prefsReport:
Wave-1 prefs is finished and all three gates are green: `pnpm -r typecheck` passes in 11 projects including prefs, `npx vitest run` passes 394 of 394 tests in 31 files, and `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs` prints "architecture rules: ok". One earlier full run had one file-level failure in `packages/sim-core/test/log-lives.test.ts`, which is W1-4's file. That file passed on its own (10 of 10) and the next full run was green, so it was a transient while another agent was editing. No git writes, no deploy, and nothing is listening on port 5311.

## Files changed

**`packages/prefs/src/`** (all new except the lead's `keymap.ts`, which I did not touch):
- **`schema.ts`** (A.2): the types, `SCHEMA_VERSION = 1` and `defineSettings`. It throws one list of every problem: duplicate id, default outside its range or options, bad field, unknown key action, reused URL parameter, a JSON default its own validator would change, a preset default that is not per drone or has no fallback. It also has `checkValue` (clamps, refuses wrong types), `PresetResolver`, `canonicalJson` and `actionsOf`.
- **`defs/*.ts`, 12 files plus `defs/index.ts`** (A.8): all 53 settings, one file per owner, and `SCHEMA` in group order. Validators for PID, rates (bounds per curve type), throttle, scene transform and folder. `DRONE_IDS`.
  - Shipped (17, everything a pilot could change in v0.2):
    - the camera: FOV and uptilt;
    - display: HUD, quality, reduced motion, F3 frame stats, language;
    - stick mode and drone choice;
    - physics: gravity, gravity mode, crash speed (vCrash), motor lag (tauMs), drag;
    - the tune: PID, rates and throttle curve.
  - Rates and throttle count because v0.2's Betaflight import sets them. The other 36 are planned.
- **`doc.ts`** (A.4): the stored document, the export file type, the four collections and their repairing validators, and the export file name.
- **`store.ts`** (A.3, A.5, A.6): `PrefsStore` and an in-memory backend that can act as a second tab.
  - Values come from the session layer, then the stored entry for the scope, then the default (a literal, the preset field, or the curated scale).
  - `set` always stores. Writes are delayed 250 ms (a slider drag still saves every 250 ms) and re-read storage first, so another tab's changes survive.
  - Every write is read back: a backend that silently drops writes, or throws, makes `writable` false.
  - A document from a newer version is read but never overwritten.
- **`migrate.ts`** (A.5): the list of all 9 v0.2 keys, a migration chain whose first step turns the v0.2 keys into the first document, and a parser for the old saved flight log. It only ever reads the old keys.
- **`io.ts`** (A.4): import planning (replace or merge), the merge rules and the `ImportReport`.
- **`url.ts`** (A.6): reads `?set.<id>=` plus the legacy `?g=`, `?gm=`, `?drone=` and `?governor=0` for the session layer.
- **`catalog.ts`** (I.1, I.2): `buildCatalogue`, shipped settings and shipped keys only. It throws, listing every missing translation per language.
- **`browser.ts`** (A.1, A.5): `LocalStorageBackend` (hears other tabs through the storage event), a read-only accessor for the old keys, `CookieValue` (same format v0.2 and the landing write), `requestPersistence` (asks once, at the first user change), `flushOnHide`, `IdbKv` (database `gsfpv` with handles, logs, blobs) and `migrateLastLog`.
  - `openBrowserPrefs(SCHEMA, resolver)` wires all of it in one call, for your "ctx.prefs is wired" step before wave 2.
- **`index.ts`**: my exports appended under the keymap line.

**Tests** (`packages/prefs/test/`): 110 new tests in 8 files (schema 12, defs 12, store 37, io 14, migrate 14, catalog 6, browser 10, architecture 5) plus `helpers.ts`, which reads the real presets from disk. They cover every A.11 unit item and I.6, each with its control.

**`scripts/check-architecture.mjs`** (shared, rule 1.4 only):
- A new check: `packages/prefs/src` may not touch window, document, navigator, location, localStorage, sessionStorage, indexedDB, matchMedia and similar, except in `browser.ts`. Comments are stripped first, because the prose says "the document (A.4)" everywhere.
- `prefs` is added to the site's list of forbidden simulator imports.

## Controls that fired
- **Architecture rule, on a temporary copy of the tree** (real sources never touched): a planted `window.localStorage` in `store.ts`, `localStorage.getItem` in `doc.ts` and `navigator.storage` in `defs/tune.ts` each exit 1. The same line in a comment, or in `browser.ts`, passes.
- **In-test controls:**
  - a global vCrash leaks between drones;
  - reset-all clears the other group;
  - a whole-document overwrite loses the other tab's value;
  - one flipped value gives exactly one preview line;
  - a missing translation throws;
  - a new storage key planted in a source file is caught by the legacy-key scan.
- **Mutation run** (`.cache/v03/w1/prefs/mutate.py`, on a copy under `.cache`): 14 of 14 fired. Each targeted test passed before its mutation and failed after. The mutations covered: two-tab merge, collection field merge, per-drone scope, write read-back, version migration, a migration writing an old key, catalogue listing planned settings, import range, merge history, reset, write delay, storing a value equal to its default, curated scale, and a changed default reaching an untouched pilot.
  - The first run caught a weak test: the two-tab test passed even with the merge broken, because the storage event hid it. I rewrote it so tab B writes before the event arrives.
- **Real Chrome** (system channel, fresh contexts, port 5311, `.cache/v03/w1/prefs/browser-probe.json`): 11 of 11 pass.
  - all 9 old keys migrate and stay untouched;
  - the old flight log lands in IndexedDB;
  - vCrash 6.5 survives leaving the page and a new tab (control: without the flush-on-hide handler it is lost);
  - two tabs through the real storage event;
  - the language cookie;
  - blocked storage gives `writable` false (control: normal storage gives true);
  - the IndexedDB round trip.
- **Language:** no Cyrillic or Polish letters in 36 files (pattern from code points, control fires). Test files also typecheck under a scratch tsconfig.

## Deviations from the design
1. `Base.action` also accepts a list, and `actionsOf()` always returns one. Reason: scene size has two keys, [ and ].
2. `PresetRef` has a `fallback` field, required on defaults, so an unknown drone never gets `undefined`. Preset JSON defaults for the tune are `null`, meaning "the preset's own values", as in `ParamOverrides`.
3. `ctx.drone` defaults to `drone.current` for both reads and writes. `no-context` is returned only for a scene setting without a scene.
4. `ui.language` has options browser / en / es / pl / ru and lives in the `NEXT_LOCALE` cookie. Setting it to `browser` deletes the cookie instead of storing it. This is the one exception to "set always stores", so the landing never sees a value it does not know.
5. **`gsfpv.lastInput` is missing from A.5's list, but v0.2 writes it.** I migrate it into a new field, `radioProfiles.last`.
6. The store writes the document at boot when none exists. That write marks the migration as done and doubles as the storage test, so the "can't save" banner can show at boot.
7. Where A.4 is silent, merges are safe to repeat: lifetime stats take the larger total, the warning flag is kept once set, scene versions take the larger number. Reset all keeps ids from newer versions.
8. The shipped-status test is written so wave 2 does not have to edit my files: v0.2 settings must stay shipped, and a new setting may ship only when its label and help exist in all four `set` language files.

## Could not do / needs you
- **I added no i18n keys**, because the prefs, set and group namespaces belong to W2-1. So the real catalogue will throw until W2-1 adds `set.<id>`, `set.<id>.help`, `set.<id>.opt.<value>`, `group.<id>`, `prefs.on`, `prefs.off`, `prefs.fromPreset` and the `keys.*` labels.
- The UI browser checks of A.11 (items 20 and 13, D-b, D-h) are W2-1's. The probe tests `browser.ts` directly.
- `persist()` answered "no" in headless Chrome, so the grant itself is unverified. The unit test proves it is called once, at the first user change.
- The probe's evidence stays in `.cache`, because `evidence/` is not my file.
- The 50 MB cap on saved logs in IndexedDB is not implemented; it belongs with W2-2's logs.
- W1-3 changed the presets during my run (`motor_idle` 0.10, `rotor_drag_per_s` added). My tests read the live preset files, so they follow W1-3's values.

Scratch files are in `C:/dev/ShramkoGSFPV/.cache/v03/w1/prefs/`:
- `browser-probe.mjs`
- `browser-probe.json`
- `mutate.py`
- `lang-check.mjs`
- `tsconfig.tests.json`

mustFix.problem: Rule 1.4 in scripts/check-architecture.mjs misses bare references to DOM and storage globals. PREFS_DOM only fires when a name is followed by '.' or '('. So `globalThis.localStorage ?? null`, `typeof window === 'undefined' ? null : window`, `globalThis.indexedDB ?? null` and `const ls = localStorage;` all pass in store.ts. The first three are the exact lines browser.ts already uses to reach storage, so moving that code into the core would not be caught. The acceptance control (a planted `window.`) fires, but the rule does not enforce what 1.4 says.
mustFix.evidence: .cache/v03/w1/review-prefs/adv-arch-browser.test.ts runs the real script on a copy of the tree. All 5 bypass lines planted in store.ts exit 0 ('architecture rules: ok'). The control, `window.localStorage` in store.ts, exits 1. .cache/v03/w1/review-prefs/rule-candidate.mjs shows a stricter pattern works: every core file comes out clean, browser.ts is hit (and is exempt), all 6 plants are caught, and a comment or string is not.
mustFix.fix: After stripping comments, also strip string literals. Then match the bare identifier: `(?<![\w$.])(window|document|navigator|location|localStorage|sessionStorage|indexedDB|matchMedia|requestAnimationFrame|HTMLElement)\b` or `\bglobalThis\s*(\.|\[)\s*["']?(window|document|navigator|location|localStorage|sessionStorage|indexedDB|matchMedia)\b`. Add the 5 bypass lines as controls in packages/prefs/test/architecture.test.ts.

mustFix.problem: Everything the first-boot migration read from v0.2 disappears from the session at the pilot's first change if the boot write failed. This happens when localStorage is full, for example when v0.2's gsfpv.lastLog nearly fills the quota. The migrated doc is never marked dirty, and flush() replays only dirty entries onto readStored(). With no gsfpv.prefs.v1 stored, readStored() returns emptyDoc. One unrelated set() then wipes stick mode, radio profiles, lastInput, favourites, filter and warned from memory, and emits them as 'external' changes. The same happens on every boot, because the doc is never written. The 'can't save' banner case is exactly where this bites.
mustFix.evidence: Unit test adv-store.test.ts ('full storage at the first v0.3 boot'): after set('flight.mode','acro') the store returns stick '2' (was '1'), radios [], favourites [], warned false. It emits external:input.stickMode, external:collection.radioProfiles, external:collection.sceneLibrary and external:collection.ui. The control run, with room for the doc, keeps everything. Real Chrome (.cache/v03/w1/review-prefs/probe.json, port 5321): the lastLog was filled to the quota minus 300 chars (quota measured at 5 242 171 b64 chars). Result: boot writable=false with stick '1' and radios [hid:pocket]; after one change stick '2', radios [], favourites []. The control, with 100 000 chars free, keeps all of it.
mustFix.fix: Keep what this tab knows until it has reached storage. Either mark every migrated settings entry and collection field dirty when the doc comes from migrateLegacy or runMigrations, until the first successful write, or remember whether this tab ever read or wrote a stored doc and use clone(this.doc) as the base in readStored() when nothing is stored and it never did. Add the quota case as a unit test, with the working-storage run as its control.

mustFix.problem: A hostile or hand-made import file can change settings without the preview or any change event showing it, and can write onto JavaScript built-ins. The settings maps are plain objects. validSettingsMap uses a spread, which keeps an own '__proto__' key. sanitize() then calls putEntry(out,'global',null,'__proto__',v), whose assignment sets the prototype of settings.global to the file's object, so entryAt() inherits its values. At drone level, the key 'constructor' makes `(s.drone[key] ??= {})[id] = v` write onto the global Object constructor. A.4 requires each value to be validated per def and previewed before it is applied.
mustFix.evidence: adv-store.test.ts, 'hostile import files'. The file {settings:{global:{"__proto__":{"physics.gravity":0,"flight.mode":"acro"}}}} gives previewImport().changes.length 0 and no onChange events, yet afterwards get('physics.gravity') is 0, get('flight.mode') is 'acro', and explicitList() lists both. Because nothing is marked dirty, flush() returns early and the hidden values stay for the session. The file {settings:{drone:{"constructor":{"physics.vCrash":9}}}} (merge) leaves Object['physics.vCrash'] === 9 and adds 1 own property to Object. Controls: the same values as plain keys are previewed (2 changes) and applied, and a real drone id stays inside the document with Object untouched.
mustFix.fix: Drop reserved keys ('__proto__', 'constructor', 'prototype') wherever a map is built from outside data: validSettingsMap, validNested, radio items, stats byDrone, versions, and in sanitize, reporting them as dropped. Read with Object.hasOwn in entryAt and in putEntry's `??=`, or build these maps with Object.create(null). Add both files above as tests.

mustFix.problem: gsfpv.lastLog is copied to IndexedDB on every boot, not 'once on the first v0.3 boot' (A.5). openBrowserPrefs calls migrateLastLog unconditionally, and migrateLastLog only checks whether the IDB key is present. The legacy key stays in localStorage for one release by design, so after the pilot erases logs (A.9 'Erase everything', or dropping the oldest under the 50 MB cap), the next boot brings the old v0.2 flight log back.
mustFix.evidence: Unit test adv-arch-browser.test.ts: after migrateLastLog, kv.delete('logs','legacy-lastLog') and a second migrateLastLog, the log is present again. The control, with no erase, copies nothing on the second call. Real Chrome (probe.json): the first boot copies it (migrated.from=0). The erase removes it (control). The next boot has migrated=null, which is not a first boot, and the log is back ('log': true).
mustFix.fix: In openBrowserPrefs, run migrateLastLog only when store.migrated?.from === 0, the boot that created the document. Or record 'lastLog moved' in the doc (for example the ui collection) and skip it afterwards. Add the erase-then-reboot case as a test.

prefsReview.notes:
I re-ran the author's checks and wrote new adversarial tests. The package is solid, but four defects need fixing before it can pass.

**What I re-ran**
- **Prefs tests:** 130 of 130 pass in 9 files. That is 110 new tests plus 20 keymap tests, well over the required 40.
- **Full test run:** `npx vitest run` passes 409 of 409 tests in 32 files.
- **Typecheck:** `pnpm -r typecheck` is green in 11 projects.
- **Architecture check:** `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs` is RED right now, but not because of prefs. It reports "sim-core touches the DOM (packages/sim-core/src/director.ts)": that file is W1-4's, edited at 19:54, and has the prose "window (" at lines 78 and 210. Rule 1 does not strip comments, so the prose trips it. The lead should tell W1-4. When the author ran it, it passed.
- **Mutation run:** I re-ran the author's `mutate.py` in my own folder (`mutate-rerun.py`): 14 of 14 controls fired, each passing before its mutation and failing after.
- **Real Chrome:** my own probe on port 5321 re-ran item 20. vCrash 6.5 survives leaving the page and a new tab; the control without `flushOnHide` loses it (4.0).
- **Language rule:** no Cyrillic or Polish letters in 36 files; the pattern is built from code points and its control fires.
- **Ports:** nothing is listening on 5321.

**Acceptance against J (W1-1)**
- 40 or more tests covering every A.11 unit item with its control: holds.
- Every v0.2 legacy key shape covered: holds. All 9 keys that v0.2 writes are in the fixture, which I checked against v0.2's `controls.ts`, `scenes/index.ts` and `main.ts`. That includes `gsfpv.lastInput`, which A.5 misses.
- The rule fails on a planted `window.` in the core: holds. But the rule is bypassable (mustFix 1).
- A.8 has all 53 settings, with the 17 from v0.2 shipped. Preset field names match `params.ts`, and every preset value lies inside its range.

**My new tests** (`.cache/v03/w1/review-prefs/`)
- **`adv-store.test.ts`, 26 tests:**
  - quota at the first boot;
  - 12 corrupted stored documents: null, array, truncated, wrong shapes, Infinity via `1e400`, deleted drone, and others. All boot, every setting reads a valid value, and the first change writes a sound document. Control: a sound stored value is used.
  - a newer version's document arriving mid-session from another tab: never overwritten, `writable` goes false. Control: a version-1 document is merged.
  - newer documents in unknown shapes;
  - hostile imports.
- **`adv-arch-browser.test.ts`, 10 tests:** the rule bypasses and the flight-log re-copy.
- **`probe.mjs` and `probe.json`:** real Chrome, 7 checks.
- **`gap-mutations.py`:** two paths no author test covers.
  - "Another tab erased everything" can be broken without any test failing.
  - "A newer document mid-session gets overwritten" also goes unseen. My test in `adv-store` covers this one, and it passes on the real code.

**Informational, not defects**
- **Two tabs, same collection field within 250 ms:** each tab adds a different radio and one is lost. The merge works per top-level collection field, and `radioProfiles.items` is one field. It is unlikely in practice.
- **The URL layer masks the pilot's changes (design-literal, A.6):**
  - With `?g=` or `?drone=` in the URL, a later `set()` stays invisible for the session: gravity set in settings still reads 1.62.
  - v0.2's drone picker wrote `?drone=` into the URL. So wave 2 must call `clearSession` on a user change, or strip the parameter after boot.
- **Scene transform defaults:**
  - `defaultOf('scene.transform')` returns null if the curated scale is 0 or less, or NaN.
  - `validateTransform` accepts any translation `t`, with no bound.
- **Catalogue wording:** a JSON default shows the "from preset" text. That will read wrong for `scene.transform` and `recording.folder` once they ship.
- **Unassigned work:**
  - The 50 MB cap on IndexedDB logs has no owner in J.
  - The `keys` namespace also has no owner.

**Deviations from the design:** all 8 are justified.
- Number 1, the action field also taking a list, changes the contract type. Consumers must use `actionsOf()`.
- Number 4, the language setting's 'browser' option deleting the cookie, is sensible.
- Number 5, migrating `gsfpv.lastInput`, fixes a gap in A.5.
- Number 6, the boot write, is fine, but it is the root of mustFix 2 when that write fails.

**What I did not re-run**
- The author's full 11-check probe: I re-ran only the item-20 check and its control.
- The IndexedDB round trip.
- The `persist()` grant: the author already reports it as unverified.

## Deviations from the design, and why

1. **Horizon keeps the rate-loop feed-forward.** Betaflight 4.5 zeroes it only in angle mode; I followed Betaflight, not the design's wording "levelled axes".
2. **The mode-switch step check covers acro→angle only.** Into horizon, the 500 ms rise delay already smooths the switch: 0.0004 per tick with and without the PT3, and 0.175 even without both. Its control cannot fire, so by the design's own rule the check is not shipped.
3. **Mode switches start from the current setpoint.** In acro the level PT3 follows the acro setpoint, so switching mode continues from where acro was. Betaflight keeps stale filter state instead; this is deterministic and removes the dependence on history.
4. **The platform gets no 1 mm skin.** With the skin, "resting produces no contact events" is false: v0.2 floors chatter about 60 events/s at 0.14 m/s. When a sphere sits exactly on the top, the disc reports the smallest positive fraction instead of 0.
5. **Rotor inertia is a preset field times a multiplier.** A.8 describes the `physics.propInertia` setting as a 0–3 multiplier. `idle` is a fraction; `physics.idlePct` needs W1-1 to divide by 100.
6. **The "unchanged terminal velocity" gate compares against duct drag 0 and the analytic value, not v0.2.** v0.2's value differs by −0.66 % only because the Pro's AUW changed from 153 to 151 g. Top speed uses a sensitivity control (CdA × 0.3), since there is no v0.2-style way to fail it.
7. **Pro II 3S duct drag is 0.6 as the design says,** although momentum-theory scaling gives 0.59. Its AUW is tagged `manufacturer` (116.2 + 42 g, both manufacturer figures). Rates are re-tagged `manufacturer` (the CLI keeps the defaults), with values unchanged, as research D1 suggests.
8. **Two fixes outside the listed deliverables, both in my files and both tested with controls:**
   - `hoverSolve().stick` is now the real stick position. v0.2 returned the curve output under that name, which is wrong with the 65/20 curve. W1-4's tests use it as a stick, so it is now correct for them.
   - Auto-throttle now maps centre stick to the mixer throttle for `hoverThr`. v0.2 gave +18 % thrust on Earth and +56 % on the Moon at centre stick.
9. **Smaller changes:**
   - Slot `S.sat` became `S.mixRange`.
   - A4's default frame is now acro: v0.2 wrote 0, which now means horizon.
   - A6 now checks the reference hash.

  - `forEachBlock` walks the octree once per 4x4x4 block using the 64-bit leaf masks. It behaves exactly like `isVoxelSolid`: it clips voxels past the grid, and a leaf or solid node above the last level covers every block below it.
  - `buildChunkFaces(col, chunk, size=32, opts?)` returns the exposed faces merged into 1-D runs, as CCW quads in world metres of the collision passed in (flip applied). It reads a one-voxel border around the chunk, so neighbouring chunks never double or drop a face.

- **`packages/collision/src/components.ts`** (new, G.1 and G.3)

## Deviations from the design
1. **Extra exports and options.** Beyond the contract I added helpers and two optional parameters: `buildChunkFaces(..., {components})`, which fills `component`, and `blockComponents(..., {connectivity})`, which the G.6 control needs. The contract signatures are unchanged.
2. **`blockIds` is not a dense grid.** It holds one id per occupied block in ascending key order, and `BlockComponents` also returns `keys`, `dims` and `connectivity`. A dense grid cannot fit: 723068d7 is 1369×2974×1495 = 6.1e9 blocks. This is my reading of "a component id per block".
3. **`ChunkMesh` meanings I chose:**
   - `faces` counts faces before merging; the number of quads is `indices.length / 6`.
   - `component` is per vertex and holds the component id; `sizes[id]` gives its size in blocks.
   - Positions are world metres of whichever collision is passed in.
4. **Format 1.1 in CI** uses the fixture's octree opened as 1.1, because the repo has no real 1.1 file. The real 887f27aa was checked in scratch only.
5. **Synthetic test worlds.** When `transformCollision` gets one of the synthetic worlds from `synthetic.ts`, the scaled world asks the original for occupancy; otherwise it would lose its walls (the `?simradio=open` test world uses these). On these worlds the mesh and components read voxel by voxel; components refuse grids above 2^21 blocks.
6. **New explicit errors:** a grid larger than its octree, or a leaf size other than 4, throws instead of silently giving different answers from `isVoxelSolid`.
7. **`mesh.ts` and `components.ts` import each other** (functions only). A separate `blocks.ts` would be cleaner, but it was not on my file list.
